vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kubernetes
Version: 2.0.0

The Kubernetes Agent Swarm bundle is a highly structured multi-agent framework for platform operations across Kubernetes and OpenShift. It utilizes seven specialized agents (Orchestrator, Cluster Ops, GitOps, Security, Observability, Artifacts, and DevEx) to manage cluster lifecycles, deployments, and security. While the agents possess high-privilege capabilities (e.g., interacting with etcd, secrets managers, and cloud CLIs), the instructions consistently enforce strict safety guardrails, human-in-the-loop approvals for destructive actions, and comprehensive audit logging (LOGS.md, SESSION.md). A 'Skill Improvement Workflow' in orchestrator/SKILL.md allows agents to propose updates via GitHub PRs, but this is explicitly designed for human review. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized persistence was found.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a coherent Kubernetes/OpenShift multi-agent operations playbook, but its runtime instructions reference many credentials, env vars, and external CLIs that are not declared—this mismatch is a security and transparency concern.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi-agent Kubernetes/OpenShift operations) aligns with the commands and capabilities documented (kubectl/oc, Helm, ArgoCD, registry, cloud CLIs). Requiring kubectl and cluster access is expected. Note: the metadata declares 'requires: kubectl' but the broader docs reference many other tools (aws, az, gcloud, jfrog, trivy, cosign, etc.) as required or optional; this is reasonable for a full platform agent but should be explicitly declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and sub-SKILLs instruct the agent to run a wide range of cluster- and registry-level commands (including create/scale/drain/cordon, registry copy/delete, ArgoCD sync/delete, cloud-provider actions). Guardrails (human-in-the-loop, 'never delete without human approval') are present, but the instructions also show how to access or manipulate credentials and registry APIs. The docs reference reading KUBECONFIG and cluster context and instruct writing to LOGS.md and MEMORY.md (expected), but they also include commands that will use env vars and secrets—these env vars and credentials are not declared in the skill metadata (see environment_proportionality).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. This is low-risk from an install/execution point of view because nothing is downloaded or written by an installer; the runtime will rely on CLIs present on the host.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The repository text references many environment variables, service credentials, and command-line credentials (examples found in the docs: KUBECONFIG, ARTIFACTORY_USER, ARTIFACTORY_TOKEN, ARTIFACTORY_URL, HARBOR_USER, HARBOR_PASS, HARBOR_URL, REGISTRY, USER, PASS, ACCOUNT, WEBHOOK_URL, az/aws/gcloud credentials and CLI actions). However, the skill metadata lists no required env vars beyond an implied kubectl binary and declares 'Required env vars: none'. This omission is significant: the runtime instructions clearly expect access to cluster credentials and third-party registry credentials. That mismatch is disproportionate and should be resolved before trusting the skill with real credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included) and model invocation allowed (normal). The skill instructs agents to append to LOGS.md, MEMORY.md, and INCIDENTS.md; persistent logging and memory is consistent with an ops skill. The skill does not request system-wide configuration changes to other skills. No elevated installer privileges are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a detailed, instruction-only operator for clusters and registries and generally matches its stated purpose — but the docs reference many sensitive env vars and credentials (KUBECONFIG, ARTIFACTORY_USER/TOKEN, HARBOR_USER/PASS, cloud CLI credentials, registry auth, webhook URLs, etc.) while the skill metadata declares none. Before installing or running: 1) Require the publisher to explicitly list all env vars/credentials the skill needs and justify each. 2) Never supply high-privilege credentials or admin kubeconfig to the skill without testing in an isolated non-production cluster first. 3) Confirm how human approvals and guardrails are enforced in your agent environment (are approvals enforced by humans or by conventions in the docs?). 4) Limit the service accounts and scopes used (least privilege) and audit LOGS.md and MEMORY.md writes. 5) If you cannot verify the exact runtime permissions and required secrets, treat this skill as untrusted for production clusters.
llm.findings: [regex-scan-none] expected: Scanner found no code-level regex hits because this is an instruction-only skill (markdown files). Absence of findings is expected but does not imply the instructions are harmless.
